news.title: The other side of China’s TNE story: China’s universities go overseas
news.summary_en: What does the opening of a new Chinese university campus in Uzbekistan tell us about the changing TNE landscape in Central Asia and China’s own overseas ambitions? David Prentice explains.
news.author: David Prentice

news.title: Carney calls for Canada to join Erasmus in push for closer EU ties
news.summary_en: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has called for Canada to join the EU’s Erasmus+ program, as he urged Brussels to build a much closer relationship with Ottawa.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Putting Pakistan on the TNE map: Beaconhouse International College and the future of global education
news.summary_en: As the international education landscape shifts, TNE offers a way to provide high-quality options for families in their home country, write Safia Cassim and Ammaar Bin Saleem.

news.title: Australia, where the bloody hell are you?
news.summary_en: Tony Burke's migration reforms show why, in international education, signals travel faster than policy.
news.author: Neil Fitzroy

news.title: OPT fee proposal clears White House review
news.summary_en: A new fee proposal for America’s post-graduation work stream has moved one step closer to implementation, after reports of the administration weighing a $100,000 charge.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Australia to restrict student dependants amid warnings of talent loss
news.summary_en: Australia’s new rules will also tighten course transfers and study progression, with education leaders warning that genuine students could choose competitor destinations.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: International student declines hit US college revenues, survey finds
news.summary_en: Nearly three-quarters of US college leaders say international student declines are squeezing institutional revenues, as federal policy actions bite.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: From refusals to looming restrictions: Five things we learned about Australia at EAIE
news.summary_en: On stage at EAIE, Phil Honeywood, CEO of the International Education Association of Australia (IEAA), offered a candid assessment of a system being reshaped by visa policy, as well as an insight into a rebranded national “vision”.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: US institutions dominate global MBA rankings
news.summary_en: US universities continue to dominate the global MBA landscape, taking the top four spots in the newly released QS Global MBA and Business Master’s 2027 Rankings.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Number of new international grad students soars in Canada
news.summary_en: A new Canadian government initiative to attract more graduate students is paying off, with the number of study permits issued to them doubling this spring compared to 2025.
news.author: Doug Ronson

news.title: US colleges restrict internships as CPT rules tighten
news.summary_en: Following two warnings from the administration last month, swathes of US colleges have suspended internship and placement opportunities for international students unless they are a degree requirement.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: EAIE: National strategies sharpen focus on talent, but autonomy stays non‑negotiable
news.summary_en: European governments are refining their internationalisation strategies with a view to attract and retain talent. But at EAIE 2026 in Glasgow, sector leaders from the UK, Germany and Slovenia underlined that universities still expect – and need – room to set their own course.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: London Mayor teams up with unis to welcome international students
news.summary_en: The Mayor of London has joined forces with London’s universities, the Metropolitan Police and Transport for London to launch a unified welcome for international students arriving in the UK's capital city.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: New Zealand’s rebound signals shift in student demand
news.summary_en: New Zealand’s international education recovery is being driven by a shift in how students view the destination, rather than simply a post-pandemic rebound, according to Education New Zealand chief executive David Downs.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Temporary win for sector in duration of status lawsuit
news.summary_en: New rules establishing strict time limits on US study visas will not begin on September 15.
